verdict.rationale: Airbyte's docs show sync scheduling (including cron) and a notification system for events plus a Connection Timeline that surfaces historical sync activity, which lets a user infer roughly how recently data was synced and get alerted on sync failures. However there is no dedicated 'freshness' metric per destination table or explicit alerting specifically when a pipeline misses its expected cadence (e.g. SLA-based staleness alerts) documented anywhere in the evidence. Missing for 10: table-level freshness/staleness indicator, explicit missed-cadence/SLA alerting feature, and any independent confirmation this works in practice.
